author: ohtadmin
title: Committee endorses limitations on parking
text:
An internal panel charged with dealing with parking and traffic has recommended restrictions on Douglas Street, Fox Run and Knowles Court.
The chief of police, Jamie Campbell, who heads the panel, presented the proposals to the town council Monday at its meeting. The next step is for the ordinance amendments to be drafted then approved for a public hearing by the councilors.
The first recommendation was to prohibit parking on Fox Run “on the easterly side of the roadway for its entire length.”
The impetus for this change was correspondence from Fox Run homeowner George Waterman, who said when “both sides are utilized, access to the cul-de-sac becomes impossible, or extremely problematic,” for delivery trucks and emergency vehicles.
Because Fox Run is the first side street heading east from Mackerel Cove that isn’t restricted, it attracts beachgoers looking for free parking, Waterman said.
Councilwoman Mary Meagher supported the proposed amendment.
“I think that’s great,” she said. “That actually means if they want to park on Fox Run, they have to go down the street and turn around. They have to make a commitment.”
The second recommendation was to restrict parking on the west side of Douglas Street between Valley and Swinburne streets.
“Given the number of driveways and fire hydrants on all three streets, the committee concluded that Douglas Street offered the most practical opportunity for effective change,” Cambpell wrote in his memo to the councilors.
The panel was tasked with studying the area around the Jamestown Arts Center and library because of the “high volume of vehicles” when the facilities are hosting simultaneous events. Fire engines, according to Campbell, cannot traverse Douglas when there is parking on both sides.
“That was a major concern,” he said.
Restricted parking on Valley and Swinburne, however, would make it onerous on the library and arts center.
“To limit parking on the other streets would essentially leave no parking at all,” Campbell said.
The final recommendation was to prohibit parking on Knowles Court on the south side for the entire length and on the north side between the intersection of Holmes Court and Coronado Street.
Campbell said parking on Knowles has been “an issue pretty much since I got here.”
“During special events, it becomes a serious concern,” he said. “It’s difficult for cars to pass through, never mind emergency vehicles.”
Campbell serves on the traffic panel with the directors of the planning, fire and public works departments, Lisa Bryer, Howie Tighe and Mike Gray, respectively.
